# Sessions

The plugin `claudetto-sessions` shows what a Claude Code session costs.
It has two reports and one note.
It works without the core plugin, and it imports nothing from another plugin.

The slices are `start-cost`, `usage`, and `awareness`.
Each report is a CLI, and a `command.run` hook shows its output with no model turn.

## Start Cost

The command `/start-cost` runs `claudetto-start`.
It reads a transcript and reports the tokens of the first request, by source: system prompt, tools, skills, agents, and memory files.
The sources are an estimate from the characters of the transcript, and the line `First request` holds the real token count.

| Exit status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | The report ran, and each bound that was given holds. |
| `1` | A bound did not hold, or `--text-max` could not run. |
| `2` | The transcript has no request with usage, so there is no data. |

- `--text-max` fails with status `1` when the transcript has no `prompt_snapshot` record.
  The report then says that the check did not run.
- `--text-min` only advises.
  It never changes the exit status.

## Usage

The command `/claudetto-sessions:usage` runs `claudetto-usage`.
It reports the model calls, the tokens that each call reads again from the cache, the cost, and the skills that a period did not use.
The built-in `/usage` is another command and runs as usual.

- Each label names one count.
  A turn is a prompt, and a call is one request to the model.
  The two counts never share a label.
- A call with a model id that has no price keeps its token counts.
  The report names the model, and its cost does not count in the total.
- The report names the Claude Code versions that the transcript records, and the version of the plugin.
- At each session start, the plugin keeps its version for the session in `$.store`, for at most 500 sessions.
  The command gives this record to the report, and the report counts the sessions of the period by plugin version.
  A session that started before the record had it counts as `not recorded`.

## Account Line

When managed settings install the plugin with `appendPlugins`, `$.session.identity()` answers.
Each report then starts with a line that names the account.
A plugin install gets a `deny` answer, and the reports name no account.

## Weekly Limit Note

Claude Code shows the rate-limit state, so the plugin does not draw it again.
When the seven-day window reaches 80 percent, the `session.measure` hook makes one note.
The main agent gets the note once, after the result of its next tool call.
The bound is `WEEKLY_WARN_PERCENT` in `slices/awareness/limits.ts`.

## Errors

Each hook of the plugin catches its errors, writes them to the debug log, and lets the session go on.
The plugin writes no stamp into the transcript.
